subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: When strict reasoning-tag stripping sees an unclosed leading `<think>` with a later `<final>` block, should OpenClaw recover only the final body, return an empty message, or keep the current post-`<think>` fallback?
rationale: This fallback is a security and message-delivery boundary: preserving text can leak hidden reasoning, while failing closed can drop user-visible answers.

options.title: Recover final body only
options.body: Use `<final>` as the trusted boundary when present and drop all preceding unclosed reasoning, then add shared and WhatsApp regression tests.

options.title: Fail closed on malformed reasoning
options.body: Return no visible text for this malformed shape, prioritizing no hidden-reasoning leakage over answer recovery.

options.title: Keep current fallback
options.body: Accept the current risk that malformed leading reasoning can be delivered when recovering otherwise-empty replies.

recommendation.title: Recover final body only
recommendation.body: Use `<final>` as the trusted boundary when present and drop all preceding unclosed reasoning, then add shared and WhatsApp regression tests.
